named, Game Boy Art School, are a collection of art from some of Blizzard’s most iconic games, like StarCraft, World of Warcraft, Diablo, and Starcraft, and have been done by a single artist for nearly 20 years. The artists began following the original art and crafting their own versions of it, and they’ve been steadily growing. The group has now gone from just one person to around 30 and has been working on the project for over 20 years.
After working with Blizzard to acquire the rights and licenses for these games, the artists started creating the art, and they’ve been doing so ever since. The entire collection has now been placed on the website, directly below the collection of Hero portraits.

One can imagine long lines of patrons snaking up the front staircase and under the the covered colonnade of Moorish arches. While they wait, they can get a glimpse of the interior through the wrought iron window bars or the thick wood balustrades on that window to the left. More table space was apparently needed at some point, so the front roof was enclosed -- like a Renzo Piano post-modern flourish -- with parts salvaged from Sky Lab.
This avant-garde design choice was slow to gain acceptance by their more conservative neighbors in the '50's ranch house and Cape Cod Revival to either side. But let's not throw stones inside glass bad houses.

extending the community feel of the laneways.
The Toowoomba CBD of five years ago is barely recognisable as a distinct family-friendly and community vibe has emerged in line with major developments such as the Walton Stores precinct.
And with that theme set to be replicated at Rowes, in the shadow of the impressive Grand Central Shopping Centre, the city centre will thrive for years to come.
Not least because of the Railway Parklands project which will extend that pedestrian feel and breath new life into a treasured piece of the city's history, and the ongoing developments in the Mills Precinct.
Changing a city's facade can come at the cost of its historic value but Toowoomba should be proud of how it has managed - so far - to honour its past but modernise and update.
There's other developments on the horizon for the CBD skyline and, with careful planning, it will ensure the city's vibrancy and viability for generations to come.
